title: Variant prototyping — telecom workshop journal
content:
Summary
This doc captures the hands-on workshop we ran with the telecom POC team (Nov–Dec 2025) focused on prototype variants for: automated ticket summarization, command-generation for device config, and conversational troubleshooting. Goal: find a minimal-cost serving strategy that meets 95th-percentile latency targets for interactive agents (p99 < 700ms streaming start) while keeping end-to-end accuracy (question-answer correctness / ticket extract quality) within 3 points of the reference full-precision baseline.

Context & constraints
- Customer environment: private VPC with burst to Dedicated (H100-backed) for heavy batches. Sensitive metadata means a Private deployment is required; redwood private control plane in customer AWS account.
- Latency SLOs: interactive assistant must begin streaming within 600–800ms for short prompts (<= 256 tokens). Batch summarization can tolerate 2–4s.
- Cost target: ~40–60% of baseline float16 hosting cost.
- Offline evaluation sets: 1. ticket-summaries (1.2k examples, ground truth summaries), 2. device-command-gen (400 examples, correctness + syntax checks), 3. conversational troubleshooting (1.5k dialog turns).

Workshop agenda (day-by-day notes)
Day 1 — kickoff & baseline collection
- Quick sync on customer intents and safety constraints.
- Baselines: float16 runs on Llama-2-13B and Mistral-7B (both hosted on A100 80GB and H100). Observed: L2-13B fp16 latency (single request, no batching) ~ p50 180ms, p95 420ms, p99 580ms (stream start measured), token throughput ~ 180 tok/s. Mistral-7B fp16 faster: p50 120ms, p95 300ms, p99 420ms, throughput ~ 270 tok/s.
- Baseline quality: L2-13B slightly better on device-command correctness (+2.6 pts), comparable on summarization and troubleshooting.

Day 2 — quantization experiments matrix design
- Variants: GPTQ (4-bit Q4_K_M), AWQ (int4 adaptive), standard int8, and mixed-precision (KV cache preserved in fp16).
- Models to test: Mistral-7B, Llama-2-13B, Mixtral-8x7B (customer liked Mixtral architecture for safety prompts).
- Hardware targets: H100 (Private customer Dedicated), A100 (fallback), CPU (low-throughput offline).
- Metrics captured: stream-start latency, p95 end-to-end, tokens/sec during generation, inference GPU memory consumption, and quality deltas vs fp16 baseline (ROUGE-L for summarization, exact-match for command syntax, dialog turn accuracy).

Day 3 — quick pass experiments (results)
- Mistral-7B Q4_K_M (GPTQ): latency improved ~25% p99 vs fp16 on H100, cost down ~46%. Quality delta: summarization -0.9 ROUGE-L, commands -1.6% exact-match, troubleshooting -1.2% accuracy.
- Mistral-7B AWQ (int4): slightly lower latency than Q4_K_M but more quality variance on longer prompts (>=512 tokens).
- Llama-2-13B GPTQ: memory reduction good, latency ~20% improvement; quality drop notable on command-gen (syntax failures ~3.8%).
- Mixtral-8x7B int8 mixed: best stability; latency gains modest (10–15%) but quality delta <1% across tasks.

Key observation: quantization method interacts with prompt length and instruction-following style. Q4_K_M robust for short interactive prompts; AWQ shows unpredictable tokenization-dependant degenerations for long device configs.

Day 4 — prompt & pipeline tuning experiments
- Prefix-caching: evaluated cache reuse for repeated device model prompts (many tickets repeat vendor strings). Prefix cache + batching reduced token cost ~18% and reduced average latency by 80–120ms for repeated workflows.
- Prompt engineering: moved static context (device specs, vendor instructions) into 1) compact structured JSON prefixed as system instruction OR 2) dynamic tool call (metadata retrieval). The tool-call approach reduced payload size to model and allowed more reliable zero-shot config generation (fewer hallucinations).
- Reranking pipeline: generate 3 candidate command outputs, run a lightweight rule-based validator (syntax + dry-run against device schema) and rerank. Reranking increased correctness from 87% -> 93% for Q4_K_M Mistral. Cost increase ~12% tokens but dramatically reduced downstream failure rate.

Day 5 — stress tests & routing policy prototype
- Hybrid routing policy: latency-sensitive interactive queries -> Mistral-7B Q4_K_M on H100; fallback to Mixtral-int8 on A100 for sustained load; very low-cost batch jobs -> CPU quantized Mixtral for nightly processing.
- Under 2x burst, Mistral Q4 maintained p95 target; under 5x burst, p99s crept up and explained failures were primarily KV-cache cold-starts and batching inefficiencies. Investigated pre-warming strategies and smarter batch shaping.

Decision log (what we recommended to the customer)
- Primary serving: Mistral-7B with GPTQ (Q4_K_M) on H100 Dedicated for interactive assistant (meets p99 targets and cost goals).
- Secondary path: Mixtral-8x7B int8 on A100 as warm fallback for overloaded Dedicated pools.
- Batch summarization & retraining jobs: Mixtral CPU-quantized int8 (offline) to minimize compute spend.
- Pipeline: generator -> validator -> reranker (3 candidates) for command-gen workflow. Validator rules owned by customer (schema + dry-run hooks).
- Prompt strategy: move stable device metadata out of model input, serve via tool-call/metadata retrieval. Use prefix caching for repeated vendors.

Open risks & mitigations
- Risk: AWQ instability for long configs could cause silent corrupt commands. Mitigation: do not use AWQ for command-gen; only consider for short interactive queries with a safety net.
- Risk: quantized variants sometimes change tokenization leading to different stop behavior. Mitigation: explicit stop tokens and shorter max_new_tokens; integrate token-level tests into CI (see linked GH-PR-1589).
- Risk: private deployment H100 capacity variability. Mitigation: multi-region Dedicated fallback and circuit-breaker that routes to reference fp16 model in hosted region for critical flows.

Operational checklist for handoff
- Infra: reserve 2 H100 instances for Dedicated pool + autoscale window configured (burst capacity at 4x).
- Monitoring: enable per-model token-latency breakdown in Console, p99 alerting at 650ms, quality regression alarms tied to eval set difference (>2% drop).
- CI: automated token-level unit tests for command syntax (GH-PR-1589) + nightly eval run on 200 holdout examples.
- Runbook excerpt: if p99 > 800ms -> first attempt: increase batch shaping limit; second: route subset of traffic to Mixtral fallback; third: increase Dedicated headroom.

Follow-ups / action items
- Marco: finalize validator rule set and convert to dry-run harness (due 2026-03-10).
- Nora: add token-level stop tests into CI and wire to nightly eval (due 2026-03-03).
- Evan: prototype pre-warm/keep-alive KV cache hook in Private deployment (due 2026-03-15).
- Asha: draft proposal for customer's ops team describing rollback & fallback policies, including costs (due 2026-03-08).

Appendix: quick numbers snapshot (H100, single-stream, median of 50 runs)
- Mistral-7B fp16: p50 120ms | p95 300ms | p99 420ms | tok/s 270 | cost baseline 1.0
- Mistral-7B Q4_K_M: p50 95ms | p95 240ms | p99 315ms | tok/s 360 | cost ~0.54
- Mixtral-8x7B int8: p50 140ms | p95 320ms | p99 430ms | tok/s 240 | cost ~0.62
- Llama-2-13B GPTQ: p50 150ms | p95 380ms | p99 470ms | tok/s 200 | cost ~0.58

Notes about reproducibility
- All quantization runs performed using customer-approved GPTQ toolchain version 1.2.0 and AWQ prototype 0.9. We saved model artifacts under private S3 bucket (links in Confluence).
- Evaluation harness: unit tests run with the same tokenizer/docker images used in Private deployment. We captured deterministic seeds and exact prompt templates in GH-PR-1589.

Unresolved questions for engineering research
- Can we implement a hybrid variable-precision KV cache (fp16 KV cache with int4 weights) in the serving runtime without significant memory overhead? If yes, expected quality improvements for AWQ could be re-opened.
- Are there quantization-aware fine-tuning gains (QAT) that give back 1–2% quality with negligible latency change? Worth investigating for command-gen-critical workflows.

End of journal.

Quick links (for reviewer)
